get.description:
Whether each active IKE_SA is actually moving packets, alongside a census of its CHILD_SAs.

This answers the question the SA listing cannot: an established tunnel that has silently stopped forwarding looks identical to a healthy one there. Sampled once a second by the statistics thread, so polling faster does not change the answer; `sample_age_seconds` exposes staleness if that thread has stopped.

An idle tunnel also reports `forwarding: false` -- that is not a fault on its own. Use `idle_seconds` together with whether traffic is expected.

post.summary: Rekey or reauthenticate a live SA
post.description:
Queue a rekey of a live SA. With `child_name`, rekeys that CHILD_SA; without it, rekeys the IKE_SA; with `reauth`, reauthenticates the IKE_SA instead, re-running authentication and re-establishing every child under a new IKE_SA.

Returns as soon as charon has queued the work -- `matched` is the number of live SAs the selector found, and zero means nothing was queued even though the request was well-formed.

AuthMethodEnum.title: AuthMethodEnum
AuthMethodEnum.description:
IKE authentication method for an auth round.

Values are the strongSwan ``auth`` keywords used in the VICI/swanctl
config. ``pubkey`` is classic X.509 mutual auth (site-to-site default);
``eap-tls`` drives remote-access (dial-up) clients with a client
certificate and is IKEv2-only, reusing the existing X.509 certificate
lifecycle. ``eap-radius`` forwards client EAP (typically username/password)
to a configured RADIUS server (see RadiusServerModel).

Password EAP without RADIUS (eap-mschapv2 against a local user DB) and
negotiated EAP (eap-dynamic) are not exposed yet.

LdapBindTypeEnum.title: LdapBindTypeEnum
LdapBindTypeEnum.description:
How the gateway locates the user entry before binding as the user.

Mirrors FortiGate's ``type``, minus ``simple``. FortiGate's ``simple`` builds
the user DN from a template and skips the search; we do not offer it for two
independent reasons. The broker (rlm_ldap) always searches and has no
DN-template mode, and against Active Directory there is no correct template
anyway -- AD's RDN is the DISPLAY name, so alice is
``CN=Alice Anderson,...``, not ``CN=alice,...``. That bites asymmetrically:
a service account created without a given/surname does have a login-shaped
RDN, so templating appears to work right up until a real user tries it.

servers.title: Servers
servers.description: Directory servers, tried in order for failover. At most 4: every extra server is another timeout one authentication can make a broker worker wait through.

security.description: Transport security. Always TLS: LDAPS (implicit, port 636) or StartTLS (upgrade on port 389). There is no plaintext option -- we bind as the user, so that would put the user's own corporate password on the wire.

ca_cert_pem.title: Ca Cert Pem
ca_cert_pem.description: PEM CA certificate used to validate the directory server's certificate. Always required. There is deliberately no option to skip certificate validation.

base_dn.title: Base Dn
base_dn.description: Base DN under which user entries are searched

username_attribute.title: Username Attribute
username_attribute.description: Attribute holding the login name (FortiGate 'cnid', Cisco 'ldap-naming-attribute'). Typically 'uid' for OpenLDAP or 'sAMAccountName' for Active Directory.

bind_type.description: How the user entry is located before binding as the user.

bind_dn.title: Bind Dn
bind_dn.description: Service-account DN used to search for user entries. Required when bind_type is 'regular'.

search_scope.description: Scope of the user search below base_dn

user_filter.title: User Filter
user_filter.description: Additional filter ANDed with the username match, e.g. to restrict to enabled accounts.

group_base_dn.title: Group Base Dn
group_base_dn.description: Base DN for group searches. Required when group_check is 'group_object' or 'posix_group'.

member_attribute.title: Member Attribute
member_attribute.description: Membership attribute: 'memberOf' on the user entry for user_attr, 'member' on the group entry for group_object, or 'memberUid' for posix_group.

group_filter.title: Group Filter
group_filter.description: Additional filter ANDed with the group-object search.

nested_groups.title: Nested Groups
nested_groups.description: Resolve nested group membership (Active Directory only). AD's memberOf lists only DIRECT membership, so a user who reaches an allowed group through an intermediate group is otherwise denied -- silently, since it looks like a legitimate authorization failure. Enabling this uses AD's LDAP_MATCHING_RULE_IN_CHAIN (1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941), which OpenLDAP does not implement; leave it off for non-AD directories.

allowed_groups.title: Allowed Groups
allowed_groups.description: Only members of these groups may connect (FortiGate 'authusrgrp'). DNs for user_attr/group_object, bare group names for posix_group. Empty means any successfully authenticated user.

timeout_secs.title: Timeout Secs
timeout_secs.description: Per-request directory timeout. Kept short so an unreachable directory fails fast instead of stalling IKE.

lockout_threshold.title: Lockout Threshold
lockout_threshold.description: Consecutive rejected credential checks, per client address and username, before the broker stops asking the directory and refuses the attempt itself (FortiGate 'auth-lockout-threshold', Cisco ASA 'max-failed-attempts'). MUST be lower than the directory's own account lockout threshold, or a password spray locks the real account out in the directory before this limiter ever trips. 0 disables the limiter and sends every attempt to the directory.

lockout_duration_secs.title: Lockout Duration Secs
lockout_duration_secs.description: How long a refused client stays refused. This is NOT the window that failures are counted in, which is set independently. There is deliberately no 'until an administrator clears it' value: the counter is held in memory on the gateway, so an indefinite lockout would be a self-inflicted denial of service with no on-box way to undo it.

eap_cert_fingerprint.title: Eap Cert Fingerprint
eap_cert_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the broker presents inside the EAP-TTLS tunnel. This is the AAA/EAP server identity, separate from the IKE gateway certificate: clients must be provisioned to expect it (strongSwan 'aaa_id', Windows 'ServerNames'), which the exported client profile does. Must have a private key on this appliance and an extendedKeyUsage of serverAuth.

eap_cert_reuse_ike.title: Eap Cert Reuse Ike
eap_cert_reuse_ike.description: Compatibility fallback: present the remote-access connection's own IKE certificate inside the tunnel instead of a dedicated EAP certificate. This lets clients that cannot be given an AAA identity connect without a profile change, at the cost of placing a copy of the gateway's IKE private key in the broker -- so a compromise of the broker becomes gateway impersonation. Off by default; only set it deliberately.

bind_password_configured.description: Whether a bind password is stored (the password itself is write-only and never returned by the API).

LdapSecurityEnum.title: LdapSecurityEnum
LdapSecurityEnum.description:
Transport security for the directory connection. Always TLS.

There is deliberately no plaintext option. We authenticate by binding as the
user, so an unencrypted connection would put the service-account password
AND every VPN user's corporate password on the wire in cleartext, and would
leave the directory's identity unverified -- meaning anything that can answer
on port 389 can harvest passwords or accept any password outright. That is
not a warning-worthy option on a security appliance; FortiGate and Cisco both
permit it and we deliberately do not.

StartTLS is the low-friction choice: it upgrades on port 389, so no new
firewall rule is needed to stop sending credentials in the clear.

Role.title: Role

Built-in RBAC roles. The set of roles is extensible; the permissions
attached to each role are decided by the server, not by this enum.

builtin.description: Built-in roles cannot be edited or deleted

RoleInfo.title: RoleInfo
RoleInfo.description: A role and the access level it grants in each feature area.

ike_proposals.title: Ike Proposals
ike_proposals.description: Ordered IKE (Phase 1) cipher proposals — encryption + integrity/PRF offered to the peer, most-preferred first. The first proposal both sides support is used to protect the IKE SA.

ike_dh_groups.title: Ike Dh Groups
ike_dh_groups.description: Ordered Diffie-Hellman / key-exchange groups for the IKE (Phase 1) SA, most-preferred first (e.g. ECP_384, MODP_4096). Sets the strength of the key exchange protecting the IKE control channel.

ike_kem_groups.title: Ike Kem Groups
ike_kem_groups.description: Additional post-quantum key-exchange methods layered onto the IKE SA per RFC 9370 (e.g. ML-KEM-768/1024), combined with the classical DH group for hybrid quantum-resistant key exchange. Up to 7 may be listed; IKEv2 only.

version.title: Version
version.description: IKE protocol version: 2 (recommended) or 1. IKEv2 is required for EAP/remote-access auth and post-quantum (RFC 9370) key exchange.

local_host.description: Local gateway address this end binds to — an IP, FQDN, or %any to accept on any local address.

local_port.title: Local Port
local_port.description: Local UDP port for IKE: 500 for native IKE, 4500 when NAT traversal (UDP encapsulation) is in use.

local_id.title: Local Id
local_id.description: Local IKE identity (IKEv2 IDi) sent to the peer — typically the subject DN of the gateway certificate, e.g. CN=gw.example.com.

local_cert_fingerprint.title: Local Cert Fingerprint
local_cert_fingerprint.description: Fingerprint selecting the local gateway certificate/key used for the local authentication round.

local_cacerts.title: Local Cacerts
local_cacerts.description: CA certificate IDs anchoring the local end's own certificate chain.

remote_host.description: Remote peer gateway address to reach (IP or FQDN), or %any to accept connections from any address (dial-up / remote-access responders).

remote_port.title: Remote Port
remote_port.description: Remote UDP port for IKE — typically 500, or 4500 with NAT traversal.

remote_id.title: Remote Id
remote_id.description: Expected IKE identity of the remote peer (IKEv2 IDr), e.g. the subject DN in its certificate. Use %any to accept any identity (common for dial-up clients matched by CA).

remote_cacerts.title: Remote Cacerts
remote_cacerts.description: Trusted CA certificate IDs used to validate the remote peer's certificate; the peer's cert must chain to one of these.

prf_alg.title: Prf Alg
prf_alg.description: Pseudo-Random Function used for IKE key derivation (e.g. PRF_HMAC_SHA2_384), usually matched to the IKE integrity algorithm.

rekey_time.title: Rekey Time
rekey_time.description: Seconds REMAINING before this live IKE SA rekeys -- not the configured interval that the same field name carries on a connection. 0 when IKE rekeying is disabled.

reauth_time.title: Reauth Time
reauth_time.description: Seconds REMAINING before this live IKE SA must reauthenticate -- not the configured interval. 0 when reauthentication is disabled.

mobike.title: Mobike
mobike.description: MOBIKE status derived from strongSwan IKE task state. This is null when the active SA view does not expose it.

fragmentation.title: Fragmentation
fragmentation.description: Enable IKEv2 fragmentation (RFC 7383). Recommended (default on): Windows/macOS/iOS native clients require it to exchange the large EAP/certificate payloads used by remote-access auth.

dpd_delay.title: Dpd Delay
dpd_delay.description: Dead Peer Detection interval in seconds — how often to check that a peer is still responsive (reclaims resources from dropped dial-up clients). 0 disables DPD.

ppk_id.title: Ppk Id
ppk_id.description: Identifier of a Post-quantum Preshared Key (PPK, RFC 8784) mixed into key derivation for quantum resistance. Optional; references a stored shared secret.

remote_access.title: Remote Access
remote_access.description: Remote-access (dial-up) connection: the gateway acts as an IKEv2 responder, assigns virtual IPs from the configured pools, and pushes configuration (DNS/routes) to connecting clients. When true the gateway acts as an IKEv2 responder assigning virtual IPs from 'pools' and pushing configuration payloads (DNS/routes) to dial-up clients.

local_auth_method.description: How this gateway proves its own identity to the peer (local IKE auth round) — typically 'pubkey' (X.509 certificate).

remote_auth_method.description: Authentication required of the remote peer/client. 'pubkey' = X.509 certificate (site-to-site); 'eap-tls' = client certificate for remote-access (dial-up); 'eap-radius' = username/password forwarded to a RADIUS server; 'eap-mschapv2' = username/password against the gateway's local user database. EAP methods require IKEv2.

pools.title: Pools
pools.description: Named virtual-IP address pools to assign to remote-access clients (gateway/responder side). Referenced by name; see PoolModel.

vips.title: Vips
vips.description: Virtual IPs to request as an initiator/client. Use '0.0.0.0'/'::' to request any address from the responder's pool.

eap_id.title: Eap Id
eap_id.description: EAP identity to use/expect for EAP authentication rounds

assigned_vips.title: Assigned Vips
assigned_vips.description: Virtual IPs assigned to a remote-access peer for this SA (from the connection's pool). Null when not a dial-up SA.

initiator.title: Initiator
initiator.description: Indicates if this is the initiator

tasks_queued.title: Tasks Queued
tasks_queued.description: List of currently queued tasks for execution

child_sa_count.title: Child Sa Count
child_sa_count.description: Number of CHILD_SAs on this IKE_SA. One per configured child is steady state; a second appears briefly around a rekey. A count that climbs and does not come down is the signature of superseded children that are never reaped.

child_sa_states.title: Child Sa States
child_sa_states.description: Census of CHILD_SA states, e.g. {'INSTALLED': 1, 'DELETED': 4}. Anything other than INSTALLED persisting here is a leak.

bytes_in.title: Bytes In
bytes_in.description: Bytes received over this IKE_SA's children

bytes_out.title: Bytes Out
bytes_out.description: Bytes sent over this IKE_SA's children

packets_in.title: Packets In
packets_in.description: Packets received over this IKE_SA's children

packets_out.title: Packets Out
packets_out.description: Packets sent over this IKE_SA's children

forwarding.title: Forwarding
forwarding.description: True when the counters above advanced recently. False on an SA that is established but moving nothing -- an idle tunnel looks the same as a broken one here, which is why idle_seconds is reported too.

idle_seconds.title: Idle Seconds
idle_seconds.description: Seconds since the counters last advanced. Null when they have not advanced since the SA was first sampled (a tunnel that has never carried traffic), which is a different thing from a tunnel that stopped.

sample_age_seconds.title: Sample Age Seconds
sample_age_seconds.description: Age of this sample. Normally 0 or 1; a large value means the statistics thread is not running and these numbers are stale.

ike_rekey_seconds.title: Ike Rekey Seconds
ike_rekey_seconds.description: Seconds until this IKE_SA is scheduled to rekey. Null when IKE rekeying is disabled. Note this is time REMAINING, unlike the identically named field on a connection, which is the configured interval.

ike_reauth_seconds.title: Ike Reauth Seconds
ike_reauth_seconds.description: Seconds until this IKE_SA must reauthenticate. Null when reauthentication is disabled. Time REMAINING, as above.

SaLivenessModel.title: SaLivenessModel
SaLivenessModel.description:
Whether a connection is actually carrying traffic, not merely established.

A connection can report ESTABLISHED with zero drops and still forward
nothing, so check these counters rather than the connection state when
traffic is missing.

Sampled by the 1 Hz statistics thread rather than on request, so two callers
a second apart see the same numbers and a caller cannot change the answer by
polling faster. ``sample_age_seconds`` says how old the sample is -- if the
statistics thread has stopped, that number grows and the rest of this record
is stale.

connection_name.title: Connection Name
connection_name.description: Name of the IKE connection whose SA to act on. Every active SA of that connection matches, so a dial-up connection with many sessions rekeys all of them; the response reports how many matched.

child_name.title: Child Name
child_name.description: Rekey this CHILD_SA of the connection instead of the IKE_SA. Omit to act on the IKE_SA.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Act on this single IKE_SA (its `uniqueid` from the SA listing) instead of every session sharing the connection name. A site-to-site connection has one session and the distinction does not arise; a remote-access connection has one per connected client, so without this a request aimed at one user's session reauthenticates all of them.

reauth.title: Reauth
reauth.description: Reauthenticate the IKE_SA rather than rekey it. Only meaningful without child_name -- charon has no notion of reauthenticating a single CHILD_SA and would silently ignore the flag, so the combination is rejected instead.

SaRekeyModel.title: SaRekeyModel
SaRekeyModel.description:
Ask charon to replace the keys on a live SA.

Three distinct operations share one request because charon's vici ``rekey``
command does, and the selector is what picks between them:

* ``child_name`` set -- rekey that CHILD_SA (a CREATE_CHILD_SA exchange that
  installs a replacement and retires the old one).
* ``child_name`` unset, ``reauth`` false -- rekey the IKE_SA (fresh keys on
  the same authenticated session).
* ``child_name`` unset, ``reauth`` true -- REAUTHENTICATE the IKE_SA: the
  peers re-run authentication from scratch and every CHILD_SA is
  re-established under the new IKE_SA.

Reauthentication otherwise happens on its own only when ``reauth_time``
elapses -- typically eight hours -- so this is the way to exercise it on
demand.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Number of live SAs the selector matched and queued work for

success.title: Success
success.description: True when charon accepted the request

message.title: Message
message.description: charon's error text when success is false

SaRekeyResultModel.title: SaRekeyResultModel
SaRekeyResultModel.description:
What charon did, not merely that the request parsed.

``matched`` is the field that matters: charon answers a selector that names
no live SA with success=no and zero matches rather than an error, so a
caller (or a test) that checks only the status code cannot tell "rekeyed"
from "there was nothing there".

SwupdateEndpointsModel.title: SwupdateEndpointsModel
SwupdateEndpointsModel.description:
The overlayable SWUpdate/registration endpoints. PUT replaces the persisted
overlay with exactly the non-null keys given, and may be refused depending on
how the device was built and licensed.

Only the endpoint locations are settable. Cryptographic trust anchors are
fixed at build time and cannot be changed through this API. `authority_ca` is
the TLS transport CA used when contacting these endpoints; it is not an
identity or image trust anchor.

otp_enforce.title: Otp Enforce
otp_enforce.description: OTP Enforcement setting for all users. When set all users must provide OTP for login.

otp_enrollment_requires_admin_token.title: Otp Enrollment Requires Admin Token
otp_enrollment_requires_admin_token.description: Require an administrator-issued single-use activation code before a user enrolling from an enrollment-scoped session can claim a second factor. Defaults on so a stolen password alone cannot register an attacker's authenticator; clear it only for a supervised fleet rollout.

token_timeout_sec.title: Token Timeout Sec
token_timeout_sec.description: Longest an issued API/UI session token stays valid (default: 30 minutes). Range 60 to 86400 seconds (1 minute to 1 day). A logout, a password change or a role change signs the session out sooner; this is the cap when none of those happen, so keep it short.

login_lockout_threshold.title: Login Lockout Threshold
login_lockout_threshold.description: Failed logins from one client address for one account before this appliance refuses further attempts for that pair, without checking the credential. Counts wrong passwords and wrong one-time passwords. Set 0 to disable the limiter and allow unlimited guessing.

login_lockout_window_sec.title: Login Lockout Window Sec
login_lockout_window_sec.description: How long a failed login is remembered. Failures older than this stop counting toward the threshold, so occasional mistakes spread over a working day never accumulate into a lockout.

login_lockout_duration_sec.title: Login Lockout Duration Sec
login_lockout_duration_sec.description: How long a lockout lasts. Attempts made during a lockout do not extend it. There is deliberately no indefinite value: an administrator locked out of the only management interface has to be able to wait it out, or log in from another address.

enable_remote_syslog.title: Enable Remote Syslog
enable_remote_syslog.description: True if remote syslog server is enabled

failed_units.title: Failed Units
failed_units.description: systemd units currently in the failed state

ordering_cycles.title: Ordering Cycles
ordering_cycles.description: True if systemd detected a unit ordering cycle at boot (causes units to be silently skipped)

services.title: Services
services.description: Per-component liveness rollup (same data as GET /sys/v1/status)

var_integrity.description: /var LUKS mount + device-identity self-report; None when unavailable

audit_logging.description: Whether the audit trail is recording. Read this field rather than inferring from log timestamps, and read it in addition to `healthy` rather than instead of it -- the two report different things.

SystemHealth.title: SystemHealth
SystemHealth.description:
Boot/runtime health the management UI surfaces. Distinct from the
per-component liveness in GET /sys/v1/status: this also captures systemd-level
boot integrity (a *skipped* unit from an ordering cycle, or a *failed* unit)
that the component list cannot express.

lockout_counter.title: Lockout Counter
lockout_counter.description: failedTries: authorization failures counted so far

max_auth_fail.title: Max Auth Fail
max_auth_fail.description: Failures tolerated before the TPM enters lockout

lockout_interval.title: Lockout Interval
lockout_interval.description: Seconds before the counter decays by one (powered on)

in_lockout.title: In Lockout
in_lockout.description: True when the TPM is refusing DA-protected objects

TpmDaModel.title: TpmDaModel
TpmDaModel.description:
The TPM's dictionary-attack accounting.

A non-zero counter is the early warning this appliance never had: the device key
is unusable once the TPM locks out, and `failedTries` is in NV so no reboot clears
it. Fields are None when the TPM could not be asked -- reporting an unreadable
counter as 0 is how a locked-out device would keep looking healthy.
